etymology: Old English greatra — larger, more weighty. The AV's comparison word for rank, light, sin, and Persons: Pharaoh's throne excepted, Jethro's confession, the Father and the Son, the indwelling Spirit over the world.
biblical_def: Greater is not a compliment contest. It is rank under God. Joseph rules the house; only in the throne is Pharaoh greater (Gen 41:40). Jethro confesses the LORD is greater than all gods (Exo 18:11). Christ says the Father is greater than I — not Arian subtraction of deity, but the Son's economic mission: He goes to the Father as the obedient Son (Joh 14:28). A greater than Solomon is here (Mat 12:42). Greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world (1Jn 4:4). God swears by no greater, so He swears by Himself (Heb 6:13). The word rebukes both egalitarian flattening and celebrity ranking. Lights differ; offices differ; the Spirit in the church is not matched by the world. Do not turn greater into self-esteem. Scripture's greater is measured from the throne down.

etymology: Old English feohtan — to fight. The AV's completed combat: Amalek at Rephidim, the LORD for Israel, stars against Sisera, Paul with beasts at Ephesus.
biblical_def: Fought is history, not metaphor first. Amalek fought Israel in Rephidim (Exo 17:8). There was no day like it, for the LORD fought for Israel (Jos 10:14). The stars in their courses fought against Sisera (Jdg 5:20). Paul fought with beasts at Ephesus — and if the dead rise not, the fight is vanity (1Co 15:32). The word will not shrink to inner struggle only. Israel had enemies with swords. Heaven fought. The apostle bled. Modern piety prefers unfought peace. Scripture records that the LORD fights, and that His people have already been in the field. Do not baptize cowardice as peacemaking. Fought is the past tense of a real war under a real Captain.

etymology: Old French plaisir — to please. The AV's verdict of delight: Balaam sees it pleased the LORD to bless; the Servant is bruised because it pleased the LORD; the Father is well pleased in the Son; fullness dwells because it pleased the Father.
biblical_def: Pleased is God's delight, not a crowd's applause. It pleased the LORD to bless Israel, so Balaam dropped his enchantments (Num 24:1). It pleased the LORD to bruise Him — penal substitution, not cosmic child-abuse theater (Isa 53:10). The voice from heaven: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased (Mat 3:17). It pleased the Father that in Him should all fulness dwell (Col 1:19). Enoch had this testimony, that he pleased God (Heb 11:5). Modern man wants God pleased with sincerity. Scripture's pleased is covenant verdict: blessing, bruising, Sonship, fullness. Do not trade the Father's pleasure in the Son for a generic self-acceptance gospel. If God is not pleased in Christ, no other smile will save.

etymology: Old English risan — to rise. The AV's completed ascent: glory risen on Zion, the Lord not in the tomb, Christ risen again at the right hand, firstfruits of them that slept.
biblical_def: Risen is the empty-tomb word. Arise, shine; the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee (Isa 60:1). He is not here: for He is risen, as He said (Mat 28:6). It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God (Rom 8:34). Now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept (1Co 15:20). The word will not stay a metaphor for inner bounce-back. If Christ be not risen, preaching is vain. Zion's light is His glory, not her mood. Do not preach risen as seasonal optimism. The grave opened; the firstfruits stand; intercession sits. Risen is history that judges every closed tomb and every spiritualized Easter.

etymology: Latin gloria + English -fy — to make glorious. The AV's completed honor: the LORD glorified among those who draw near; the Son of man glorified; the finished work; the God of the fathers glorified His Son Jesus.
biblical_def: Glorified is honor publicly set on God and on the Son. I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified (Lev 10:3) — Nadab and Abihu learned it in fire. The hour is come that the Son of man should be glorified (Joh 12:23) — the cross, not a platform. I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work (Joh 17:4). The God of Abraham hath glorified His Son Jesus, whom ye delivered up (Act 3:13). Modern talk of being glorified is influencer light. Scripture's glorified is holiness made visible, the hour of the cross, finished work, and apostolic preaching of the raised Son. Do not steal the verb for self-branding. God is glorified when nearness is holy and the Son is not denied.

etymology: Greek propheteuo via Latin — to speak forth. The AV's completed speech: the seventy, Saul among the prophets, Micah in Hezekiah's days, the law and the prophets until John.
biblical_def: Prophesied is speech that already happened under God, not a talent show. When the Spirit rested on the seventy, they prophesied and did not cease (Num 11:25). The Spirit of God came upon Saul, and he prophesied among them (1Sa 10:10). Micah prophesied in the days of Hezekiah: Zion shall be plowed (Jer 26:18). All the prophets and the law prophesied until John (Mat 11:13). The word is past because the speech was given. Modern platforms sell prophesied as content calendar. Scripture's prophesied is Spirit-rest, royal disruption, covenant lawsuit, and the close of the old prophetic line at the Baptist. Do not confuse ecstatic noise with the office. False prophets also spoke. The test is the LORD's word coming to pass, and Christ as the end of the line they served.

etymology: Old French apointer — to fix, assign. The AV's assignment word: a place of refuge, Levites over the tabernacle, seven over business, a set time remembered.
biblical_def: Appoint is God's fixing of place, office, and time — not a committee vibe. I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee (Exo 21:13). Thou shalt appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of testimony (Num 1:50). Look out seven men... whom we may appoint over this business (Act 6:3). Appoint me a set time, and remember me (Job 14:13). The word will not flatten into self-appointment. Cities of refuge are appointed. Levites are appointed. Deacons are appointed. Death itself is appointed (Heb 9:27, appointed unto men once to die). Modern leadership talk loves volunteer energy. Scripture loves assignment. Do not seize an office God did not appoint. Do not refuse a place He did.

etymology: Old English strengthu — force, firmness. The AV's completed fortifying: Jonathan strengthened David's hand in God; Ezra strengthened as the LORD's hand was upon him; inner man strengthened with might; all might according to His glorious power.
biblical_def: Strengthened is gift, not self-talk. Jonathan went to David in the wood and strengthened his hand in God (1Sa 23:16) — friendship as means, God as object. Ezra was strengthened as the hand of the LORD his God was upon him (Ezr 7:28). Paul prays they be strengthened with might by His Spirit in the inner man (Eph 3:16), strengthened with all might according to His glorious power (Col 1:11). The word rebukes both stoic grit and therapeutic affirmation. David's hand is strengthened in God, not in a mirror. Inner man is Spirit-might, not self-esteem. Do not preach strengthened as hustle. The wood, the king's court, the inner man, and patience with joyfulness are all the same doctrine: God puts strength where He puts His hand.
